result.summary: Do not ship: explicit measurement references still allow foreign verification to leak, and whole dataset corrections can lose applicable assumptions.

findings.title: Include explicit measurement references in assumption ancestry
findings.body: Admission ignores the original assumption’s measurement_ref. In a schema-valid mixed-subject run, an assumption referencing model B becomes eligible because its owner also contains model A. Replacing it with an assumption referencing A emits status: verified after B’s measurement is excluded. Embedded assumptions similarly bypass isolation when their containing measurement belongs to A but measurement_ref identifies B. Live emission, corpus reference checks and pinned replay all accept these reproductions.
findings.recommendation: Resolve original assumptions’ measurement_ref using exact raw-owner rules and enforce that measurement’s subject ancestry throughout applicability propagation, alongside containment checks. Add mixed-subject run-level and embedded regressions.

findings.title: Preserve historical dataset bindings for whole-replacement ancestry
findings.body: Replacing an old owner’s sole associated dataset measurement leaves no usable historical anchor: retaining its association fails _dataset_associations with 'no exact active evidence', while removing it excludes the original from measurement_anchors. With identical MTZ subjects and a valid successor association, the working tree silently drops A_corrected_dataset while emitting its measurement; committed admission retains the assumption. Legitimate corrections therefore cannot preserve these assumptions through retirement.
findings.recommendation: Validate historical dataset bindings against raw targets for ancestry separately from active association admission, preserving exact owner and selector checks. Add whole-replacement and retired-owner dataset regressions.

next_steps: Fix both admission gaps and exercise them through live emission, corpus checks and pinned replay. The reported test counts, old-admission mutation failures and real byte-identical output were independently reproduced; file-writing tests used in-memory I/O.
